stem: A newly rooted propagule wilts after being moved abruptly from a high-humidity propagation environment into much drier air. What is the best corrective approach?
choices: Return it to a protected transition environment and reduce humidity gradually while maintaining appropriate root-zone moisture
Increase fertilizer concentration immediately so the plant takes up more water
Allow the root zone to dry completely to force faster adaptation
Remove most of the new roots so shoot water demand falls
rationale: Newly rooted propagules benefit from gradual acclimatization as transpiration demand and root water uptake capacity rebalance; an abrupt humidity drop can produce wilting before the plant is adapted.
